name: Amara Okafor
presenting_complaint: Lower abdominal pain and light vaginal bleeding at 7 weeks by dates

medical_history.social: Administration officer. Non-smoker. In a stable relationship. Last menstrual period 7 weeks ago.

validation_criteria.presenting_scenario: A 29-year-old woman, 7 weeks by LMP, presents with left iliac fossa pain and light vaginal spotting for one day. She has a positive urine pregnancy test, a history of prior PID and is blood group O Rh-negative. Obs: BP 104/64, HR 104, RR 18, afebrile, GCS 15. She is mildly tender in the left iliac fossa. She has not had a scan this pregnancy.
validation_criteria.task: Document your assessment and initial management as the admitting RMO.

subjective: Confirm pregnancy and dates (LMP 7 weeks, positive urine hCG); ask about prior scan this pregnancy
Characterise pain: site (left iliac fossa), onset, severity, radiation to shoulder tip (diaphragmatic irritation)
Vaginal bleeding: amount, clots, products of conception passed
Ectopic risk factors: previous PID/chlamydia, prior ectopic, tubal surgery, IUD, IVF, smoking
Screen for haemodynamic/rupture symptoms: dizziness, syncope, shoulder tip pain
Obstetric history: G3P1, one prior miscarriage; ask blood group (O Rh-negative)
objective: Vital signs and assessment for shock (HR 104, borderline BP — watch trend)
Abdominal exam: left iliac fossa tenderness, guarding/rebound, peritonism suggests rupture
Speculum and bimanual: assess bleeding, cervical os (open/closed), cervical motion tenderness, adnexal tenderness/mass
Quantitative serum beta-hCG (baseline, with plan to repeat in 48 h if pregnancy of unknown location)
Transvaginal ultrasound to locate the pregnancy (intrauterine vs adnexal mass / free fluid)
FBC, group and hold / crossmatch, confirm Rh status; correlate hCG with the discriminatory zone
assessment: Primary working diagnosis: Ectopic pregnancy / pregnancy of unknown location (PUL) until an intrauterine pregnancy is confirmed — must NOT default to benign miscarriage
Document ectopic as the must-exclude diagnosis given LIF pain, risk factors and no confirmed intrauterine pregnancy
Differentials: threatened/incomplete miscarriage, corpus luteum/ovarian cyst, appendicitis, PID — but ectopic excluded first
Assess for signs of rupture (haemodynamic instability, peritonism, shoulder tip pain)
plan: Quantitative serum beta-hCG now and transvaginal ultrasound to locate pregnancy; if PUL, repeat beta-hCG in 48 hours and follow a defined PUL pathway
Anti-D immunoglobulin 250 IU IM given she is Rh-negative with bleeding in early pregnancy
Two large-bore IV cannulae, FBC and group and hold/crossmatch; keep nil by mouth if surgery likely
Urgent gynaecology referral; if haemodynamically unstable or ruptured — resuscitate and arrange emergency laparoscopy/laparotomy (salpingectomy/salpingostomy)
If stable, unruptured, meeting criteria: discuss expectant vs medical (methotrexate) vs surgical management with gynaecology
Analgesia and antiemetic; serial observations for deterioration
Clear safety-netting: return immediately if worsening pain, dizziness, heavy bleeding or shoulder tip pain; documented follow-up and disposition

critical_errors: Defaulting to a benign miscarriage diagnosis and discharging without excluding ectopic — no documented beta-hCG and transvaginal ultrasound / PUL pathway
Failing to give anti-D immunoglobulin to this Rh-negative woman with early-pregnancy bleeding
Not recognising or acting on signs of ectopic rupture (shoulder tip pain, peritonism, rising HR) and delaying resuscitation/surgical referral
Sending the patient home without gynaecology referral, follow-up beta-hCG or safety-netting
must_not_miss: Ectopic pregnancy excluded via beta-hCG plus transvaginal ultrasound (or formal PUL pathway) before attributing symptoms to miscarriage
Anti-D given because the patient is Rh-negative
Ruptured ectopic recognised and escalated for emergency surgery if unstable
